cohort: 634 Syrian refugee women and 21,092 Turkish resident women who gave birth at a hospital in Aydin, Turkey, between October 1, 2009, and June 1, 2019
finding: While Syrian refugee women had lower maternal age, higher adolescent pregnancy and parity rates, and lower antenatal screening test attendance, their obstetric and neonatal outcomes were comparable to Turkish resident women.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rate was higher among Turkish residents overall, but the rate of primary cesarean section was similar between groups; however, cesarean section due to previous repetitive cesarean delivery was significantly higher in the refugee group.
